prompt: A battery log on your phone reads: hour $1 \to 88\%$, hour $3 \to 64\%$. What is the rate of change in percent per hour? (Include the sign.)
hint: The battery is DRAINING, so the rate should come out negative.

hints.text: The battery is DRAINING, so the rate should come out negative.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler log: $80\%$ at hour $1$ and $70\%$ at hour $2$ drops $10$ over $1$ hour = $-10$ per hour. Find the drop, then divide by the hours.
Change in percent: $64 - 88 = -24$. Change in hours: $3 - 1 = 2$.

explanation: Slope $= \frac{-24}{2} = -12$: the battery loses $12\%$ each hour.

alternativeExplanations.title: Fill the missing hour
steps: From hour $1$ to hour $3$ the battery fell $24\%$ over $2$ hours — split it evenly.
Hour $2$ must read $76\%$: each hour drops $12$, so the rate is $-12$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Dividing by 3 — the hour on the clock — instead of the 2-hour GAP gives −8, a neat wrong answer.
Slope uses the change in time, not the time itself: from hour 1 to hour 3 is 2 hours. −24 ÷ 2 = −12% per hour.
